summary: Opaque prebuilt native addon with credential-lookup, host-recon, and process-spawn capabilities; unverifiable parent package
details: Package `new-native-tools-linux-x64-gnu` ships only a ~10 MB Linux x64 Node native addon (`.node` file) directly referenced by `main`, with a one-line README and no wrapper JavaScript. Strings recovered from the binary include credential-lookup markers (`Found login for`, `SQLITE_AUTH_USER`), host reconnaissance paths (`/dev/disk/by-id/`, `/etc/lsb-release`, `network_adapters`, hostname and interface enumeration), an embedded Rust HTTP/TLS client (`ureq_proto::util`), ChaCha20 cryptographic primitives, and process-spawn primitives (`posix_spawnp`, `execvp`). The package name and versioning scheme (`3.1.40-browser-release-151-371-1784887043`) impersonate a platform-specific artifact of a parent package, but no legitimate parent publishes this native addon at these coordinates. The capability set — SQLite credential reads, browser-login-shaped string tables, disk/host identity collection, an HTTP client, and shell-exec primitives bundled into a single opaque Linux binary loaded when the module is required — matches the shape of a credential/browser stealer for the installer's host. No install lifecycle hook is present, so harmful code fires when a consumer requires the module rather than on `npm install`.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
